subject: Re: ACME — SLO / SLA language + latency measurement
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <echen@acme.com>, George Patel <gpatel@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: SLO targets and SLA language (post-demo)

Hi Emily / George —

Thanks again for the time earlier today. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can lock the SLA language and run the proof-of-performance tests next week.

Recap (what we heard)
- Target p95 latency: <= 200ms for chat/text generation up to 512 tokens (single-turn).
- Concurrency target: support sustained 50 concurrent requests (concurrency defined as concurrent in-flight requests per model instance).
- Throughput: account-level baseline 1k req/min with ability to burst to 2k req/min for 10 minutes.
- Streaming: first-token latency important — want sub-100ms first token for streaming responses.
- Reporting cadence: weekly during onboarding, monthly thereafter.

Clarifying questions / asks from Redwood:
1) Latency measurement: can you confirm whether ACME expects latency measured end-to-end from client-to-client, or server-side (Redwood ingress to final token delivered)? We typically measure ingress->egress at our edge by default and provide a client-side SDK hook if you need client-to-client.
2) Exclusions: are scheduled maintenance windows and third-party network outages acceptable exclusions for SLA breaches?
3) Remedies: do you have a preferred remedy structure (service credits cap, remediation timelines)? Our standard is tiered credits up to a cap (we included draft language in the attached PDF).
4) Proof-of-performance: we can run a canary test (10k requests over 24 hours) and share raw logs and the performance_test_summary.csv — ok to proceed next Tue/Wed?

I've attached draft SLA language (redwood_sla_draft_v2.pdf) and a sample performance summary to show how we report p50/p95/p99 and first-token for streaming. If you want, Rishi can jump on a short call to walk legal + infra team through the exact measurement points.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm measurement preference and exclusions by EOD Wed 10/20
- We run the 24-hr canary Tue 10/26 and share results by 10/27
- Legal review concurrent with canary; iterate SLA language as needed

Thanks — looking forward to locking this down.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0189

Attachment: redwood_sla_draft_v2.pdf

From: Emily Chen <echen@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: George Patel <gpatel@acme.com>, ACME Legal <legal@acme.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T09:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: SLO targets and SLA language (post-demo)

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few quick answers and clarifications from our side:

1) Measurement: ACME prefers an end-to-end measurement if possible (client request => final token received by client). That said, we understand client-side variability; if Redwood can provide both server-side ingress->egress and a client-side SDK measurement, that would be acceptable. Please flag any known skew drivers.

2) Exclusions: Scheduled maintenance is fine as an exclusion. We also want to exclude force majeure and upstream cloud provider outages. We expect Redwood to notify us at least 2 hours in advance for planned maintenance that could impact the SLA.

3) Remedies: Our legal team prefers a capped credit approach rather than automatic termination. Typical starting point for us is credits up to 10% of the monthly invoice, with clear thresholds and an SLA reporting cadence.

4) Streaming: Confirming streaming first-token latency is critical for our UX. We also need the ability to limit per-session concurrent streams (we will provide expected session concurrency distributions).

5) Proof-of-performance: Tue/Wed next week works for a canary. Please include the raw logs and a CSV with per-request timings.

I'll loop legal (legal@acme.com) once we get the Redwood response on exact measurement definitions.

—Emily
Emily Chen
Infrastructure Lead — ACME Corp
echen@acme.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <echen@acme.com>, George Patel <gpatel@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: SLO targets and SLA language (post-demo)

Hi Emily / George — thanks for the clear feedback. Below is how Redwood proposes to operationalize the measurements and SLA language (we can iterate based on legal feedback):

Measurement definitions (we will provide both server-side and client-side metrics):
- Server-side (default for SLA calculations): time from request arrival at Redwood ingress (timestamp at our edge) to final token streamed to Redwood's egress point. This is measured in ms per-request and aggregated to p50/p95/p99 for the billing period.
- First-token streaming latency: measured from ingress to first-byte available to the client; reported separately as a p50/p95 metric.
- Client-side measurement: we will provide an SDK hook (optional) that reports client-observed times. Client-side metrics are provided for diagnostic purposes and are not used for credit calculations unless both parties agree to a client-side baseline during onboarding.

Exclusions and maintenance windows:
- Scheduled maintenance: excluded if Redwood provides >=2 hours notice and the window is documented in the monthly incident report.
- Upstream provider outages and force majeure: excluded with incident documentation.
- Customer-induced outages (e.g., malformed traffic, authentication failures) are excluded.

Reporting cadence and evidence:
- Onboarding: weekly reports (per-request CSV + aggregate p50/p95/p99 + first-token stats) for the first 30 days after go-live.
- Ongoing: monthly SLA reports with monthly aggregates and incident notes.
- For disputed incidents we will share raw logs (redacted for PII) within 3 business days.

Remedies:
- Service credits tiered by monthly availability and latency targets. Example: if monthly p95 latency target missed by >20% yield X% credit, etc.
- Total remedies capped at 10% of the affected month's invoice (we are ok to include that cap; see attached draft language).

Proof-of-performance / canary
- Proposed canary: 24-hour run starting Tue 2026-10-26 00:00 UTC, ~10k requests, 50 concurrent simulated sessions, include streaming flows.
- Deliverables: per-request CSV (performance_test_summary.csv), aggregate report, and a short debrief call the next day.

We're attaching the performance_test_summary.csv and the updated SLA draft (redwood_sla_draft_v2.pdf) with the measurement language filled in. If legal requests small wording changes (e.g., explicit mention of SDK vs server-side acceptance), we can accommodate.

Let us know if the canary timing works and who from ACME infra/legal should be on the debrief.

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Solutions & Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

From: Emily Chen <echen@acme.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: George Patel <gpatel@acme.com>, ACME Legal <legal@acme.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: SLO targets and SLA language (post-demo)

Thanks Rishi — that all sounds good and aligns with our expectations. A couple of small asks from legal before we sign:

- Please add an explicit sentence that client-side SDK metrics are "diagnostic only" unless both parties sign off to use them for credit calculations.
- Keep the remedies cap at 10% of monthly fees (we've noted that in the email thread; legal will insert exact thresholds).

We approve the canary for Tue 2026-10-26; please proceed. For the debrief, please include: me (Emily), George (infra), and our legal rep (legal@acme.com).

Can we get a mutual action plan (table of dates/owners) in a short doc so procurement has visibility? If you can share a DocuSign link after legal sign-off that would be great.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Emily
Emily Chen
Infrastructure Lead — ACME Corp
echen@acme.com
